newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Arafat bitterly complains of Israeli actions.
newsitem.headline: Arafat bitterly complains of Israeli actions.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat complained bitterly on Sunday that Israel was breaking peace agreements, dragging its feet on solving disputes and crippling the Palestinian economy.
Arafat told the World Economic Forum in the Swiss town of Davos the Palestinians had fulfilled their side of the bargain but the new Israeli government had not done likewise.
"We have kept up our side of the agreement and exerted all possible efforts to resume the negotiations with the new Israeli government to implement the interim agreement," he said.

"The problem we face today is the procrastination with which Israel is implementing its part of its agreement and the failure to solve several pending problems though they are vital and important," he added.

"Attempts are being made to evade or not to attend those meetings of committees set up to solve basic and important questions... Part of this was the failure (by Israel) to pay our share of taxes levied by the Israeli government -- these amounted to hundreds of millions of dollars," he said.

Arafat, who met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Davos on Sunday and agreed to meet him again on Thursday, complained that Israel continued to confiscate Arab land and build Jewish settlements. "Other serious violations have been committed," he added.
Switching from Arabic to English to make his point clearer, he added:

"When I say it (Israel's settlement policy) is illegal, it is according to U.N. resolutions, it is according to the letter of guarantees which we received at the Madrid conference (in 1991) and signed by Mr (U.S. secretary of state James) Baker and according also to the agreement that we signed."
Arafat said Israeli restrictions of the movement of people and goods between Israel and the Palestinian territories was costing Palestinians $7 million a day.
Palestinian national income had fallen 35 percent in 1996 from 1995 and private investment in the territories had slumped to $250 million from $700 million, he added.
"Is this a just peace? Is this the peace expected by the world? Our nation is the only one paying a price for peace. Our nation is paying a harsh price," he said.

The Palestinian leader also aired his grievances that Israel is preventing Palestinians from using Gaza airport or starting work on Gaza seaport and has failed to put into effect an old agreement on a safe passage between Gaza and the West Bank.
Arafat greeted, praised and welcomed former Israeli prime minister Shimon Peres, who was present in the audience, but did not mention by name his successor, Benjamin Netanyahu.

Netanyahu was the next speaker in a World Economic Forum session on the Middle East. Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak spoke earlier. The three leaders appeared in succession, each leaving the hall before the next appeared.
